convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator WPRSIsignal and depends on TradeAlgorithms.mqh external library for all trade execution, position sizing, and close logic. Custom indicator logic is opaque and cannot be auto-converted without reimplementing the indicator.

derived_values.name: FilterMax - maximum filter width plus buffer
min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator warmup
UpSignalTime - timestamp for buy signal identification
DnSignalTime - timestamp for sell signal identification

other_exits: Historical close-signal search: when both open and close are enabled for same side but no close signal found on SignalBar, EA searches forward through bars (SignalBar+1 onward) for an opposing signal to set BUY_Close or SELL_Close

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lots at MM value; FREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin; BALANCE=MM fraction of balance; LOSSFREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin minus loss; LOSSBALANCE=MM fraction of balance minus loss

custom_logic_notes: Entry and close signals are gated by input booleans (BuyPosOpen, SellPosOpen, BuyPosClose, SellPosClose) allowing independent enable/disable of each direction. When SignalBar=0, signals are evaluated every tick instead of on new bar. The historical close-signal search loop (bars SignalBar+1 onward) is only triggered when both open and close are enabled for a side pair and no close signal was found on the current SignalBar. Trade execution functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar) all come from TradeAlgorithms.mqh and their internal logic is opaque. Signal time is used by trade functions likely to prevent duplicate entries on the same signal bar.
python_conversion_notes: The WPRSIsignal custom indicator must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented in Python. The indicator likely combines WPR (Williams Percent Range) and RSI with filter thresholds for buy/sell zones. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library handles all position management including margin-based lot sizing, position open/close with signal-time dedup, and global variable cleanup - all of this must be reimplemented. The historical close-signal search loop adds complexity: when no close signal exists on SignalBar, it scans forward bars for an opposing signal to determine if a close should occur. SL/TP of 1000/2000 points suggest these are point values (not pips), which at 5-digit would be 100/200 pips - verify digit adjustment logic in TradeAlgorithms.mqh.
